1ca3632b3ee2d25d.claim: In a secular model of detached trans-Neptunian objects (giant-planet quadrupole, Galactic tide, the QUMOND anomaly), the EFE's quadrupole drives large perihelion changes; with the external field remov
1ca3632b3ee2d25d.note: The 0.00485 AU is check C2: a monopole-only K1 run with planets AND tide switched off, over 200 Myr, compared with Newton. It is a numerical check that a central force conserves q, not 'the external field removed' in the full model described (planets + tide + QUMOND); with the tide on, perihelia do change. The EFE runs do move q a lot: K1 lost 0.573 vs Newton 0.187, detached occupancy 0.195 vs 0.067. But the pre-registered p57 decision was INCONCLUSIVE, and the paper does not say so.

e730c96b98c4946d.section: What an EFE-free rule costs and predicts
e730c96b98c4946d.claim: \section{What an EFE-free rule costs and predicts} Two results in this programme preferred an EFE: the Milky Way's Gaia DR3 outer decline (the isolated kernel is $2.5\sigma$ shallower; disequilibrium
e730c96b98c4946d.note: 'WALLABY gives -1.7 sigma' is wrong. -1.70 is the stacked AMPLITUDE A_hat = -1.70 +- 2.12 (Z = -0.57) of the directional-EFE asymmetry test, in units where AQUAL = +1. It is consistent with AQUAL; the sensitivity is ~0.3 sigma at AQUAL amplitude and the output says no verdict is possible. The direct Chae-type WALLABY test (h28) gives +0.4 sigma and is recorded as UNDERPOWERED. Other numbers: Chae 1.7-2.2 / 2.7-3.0 sigma match CFG8, but they mix two kernels (P2 = this law gives 1.7 / 2.7; nu_mono gives 2.2 / 3.0), so 'refitted with this law' is loose. MW 2.5 sigma is the extreme of L172's range (nominal slope -0.126/-0.117 gives 2.3/2.4 sigma), computed with the nu_RAR kernel, not this law. L172's 1-D LMC field model puts it at 1.1-1.6 sigma.
